   297→    def build_tokenized_answer(self, prompt, answer):
   298→        """
   299→        Llama tokenizer does satisfy `enc(a + b) = enc(a) + enc(b)`.
   300→        It does ensure `enc(a + b) = enc(a) + enc(a + b)[len(enc(a)):]`.
   301→        Reference:
   302→            https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/pull/531#issuecomment-1595586257
   303→        """
   304→
   305→        full_tokenized = self.tokenizer(prompt + answer, add_special_tokens=False)
   306→        prompt_input_ids = self.tokenizer(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
   307→
   308→        answer_input_ids = full_tokenized["input_ids"][len(prompt_input_ids) :]
   309→        answer_attention_mask = full_tokenized["attention_mask"][len(prompt_input_ids) :]
   310→
   311→        # Concat tokens to form `enc(a) + enc(a + b)[len(enc(a)):]`
   312→        full_concat_input_ids = np.concatenate([prompt_input_ids, answer_input_ids])
   313→
   314→        # Prepare input tokens for token by token comparison
   315→        full_input_ids = np.array(full_tokenized["input_ids"])
   316→
   317→        if len(full_input_ids) != len(full_concat_input_ids):
   318→            raise ValueError("Prompt input ids and answer input ids should have the same length.")
   319→
   320→        # On some tokenizers, like Llama-2 tokenizer, there are occasions where tokens
   321→        # can be merged together when tokenizing prompt+answer. This could result
   322→        # on the last token from the prompt being different when tokenized on its own
   323→        # vs when done as prompt+answer.

   327→        # last token has changed due to merging.

   354→        We also create the labels for the chosen/rejected responses, which are of length equal to
   355→            the sum of the length of the prompt and the chosen/rejected response, with
   356→            label_pad_token_id  for the prompt tokens.
   357→        """
   358→        batch = {}
   359→        prompt = feature["prompt"]
   360→        chosen = feature["chosen"]
   361→        rejected = feature["rejected"]
   362→
   363→        if not self.is_encoder_decoder:
   364→            # Check issues below for more details
   365→            #  1. https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/907
   366→            #  2. https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/pull/531#issuecomment-1595586257
   367→            #  3. https://github.com/LianjiaTech/BELLE/issues/337
   368→
   369→            if not isinstance(prompt, str):
   370→                raise ValueError(f"prompt should be an str but got {type(prompt)}")
   371→            prompt_tokens = self.tokenizer(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
   372→            prompt_tokens = {f"prompt_{k}": v for k, v in prompt_tokens.items()}
   373→
   374→            if not isinstance(chosen, str):
   375→                raise ValueError(f"chosen should be an str but got {type(chosen)}")
   376→            chosen_tokens = self.build_tokenized_answer(prompt, chosen)
   377→
   378→            if not isinstance(rejected, str):
   379→                raise ValueError(f"rejected should be an str but got {type(rejected)}")
   380→            rejected_tokens = self.build_tokenized_answer(prompt, rejected)
   381→
   382→            # Last prompt token might get merged by tokenizer and
   383→            # it should not be included for generation if that happens
   384→            prompt_len_input_ids = len(prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   385→
   386→            chosen_prompt_len_input_ids = len(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   387→            rejected_prompt_len_input_ids = len(rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   388→            prompt_len_input_ids = min(chosen_prompt_len_input_ids, rejected_prompt_len_input_ids)
   389→
   390→            for k, v in prompt_tokens.items():
   391→                prompt_tokens[k] = v[:prompt_len_input_ids]
   392→
   393→            # Make sure prompts only have one different token at most an
   394→            # and length only differs by 1 at most
   395→            num_diff_tokens = sum(
   396→                [a != b for a, b in zip(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"], rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])]
   397→            )
   398→            num_diff_len = abs(chosen_prompt_len_input_ids - rejected_prompt_len_input_ids)
   399→            if num_diff_tokens > 1 or num_diff_len > 1:
   400→                raise ValueError(
   401→                    "Chosen and rejected prompt_input_ids might only differ on the "
   402→                    "last token due to tokenizer merge ops."
   403→                )
   404→
   405→            # add BOS token to head of prompt. Avoid adding if it's already there
   406→            bos_token_id = self.tokenizer.bos_token_id
   407→            if prompt_len_input_ids == 0 or bos_token_id != prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"][0]:
   408→                prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"] = [bos_token_id] + prompt_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]
   409→                prompt_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"] = [1] + prompt_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"]
   410→            if chosen_prompt_len_input_ids == 0 or bos_token_id != chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"][0]:
   411→                chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"] = [bos_token_id] + chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]
   412→                chosen_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"] = [1] + chosen_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"]
   413→            if rejected_prompt_len_input_ids == 0 or bos_token_id != rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"][0]:
   414→                rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"] = [bos_token_id] + rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]
   415→                rejected_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"] = [1] + rejected_tokens["prompt_attention_mask"]
   416→
   417→            # add EOS token to end of answer. Avoid adding if it's already there
   418→            eos_token_id = self.tokenizer.eos_token_id
   419→            if len(chosen_tokens["input_ids"]) == 0 or eos_token_id != chosen_tokens["input_ids"][-1]:
   420→                chosen_tokens["input_ids"].append(eos_token_id)
   421→                chosen_tokens["attention_mask"].append(1)
   422→            if len(rejected_tokens["input_ids"]) == 0 or eos_token_id != rejected_tokens["input_ids"][-1]:
   423→                rejected_tokens["input_ids"].append(eos_token_id)
   424→                rejected_tokens["attention_mask"].append(1)
   425→
   426→            longer_response_length = max(len(chosen_tokens["input_ids"]), len(rejected_tokens["input_ids"]))
   427→
   428→            # if combined sequence is too long, truncate the prompt
   429→            for answer_tokens in [chosen_tokens, rejected_tokens, prompt_tokens]:
   430→                if len(answer_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]) + longer_response_length > self.max_length:
   431→                    if self.truncation_mode == "keep_start":
   432→                        for k in ["prompt_input_ids", "prompt_attention_mask"]:
   433→                            answer_tokens[k] = answer_tokens[k][: self.max_prompt_length]
   434→                    elif self.truncation_mode == "keep_end":
   435→                        for k in ["prompt_input_ids", "prompt_attention_mask"]:
   436→                            answer_tokens[k] = answer_tokens[k][-self.max_prompt_length :]
   437→                    else:
   438→                        raise ValueError(f"Unknown truncation mode: {self.truncation_mode}")
   439→
   440→            # if that's still too long, truncate the response
   441→            for answer_tokens in [chosen_tokens, rejected_tokens]:
   442→                if len(answer_tokens["prompt_input_ids"]) + longer_response_length > self.max_length:
   443→                    for k in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]:
   444→                        answer_tokens[k] = answer_tokens[k][: self.max_length - self.max_prompt_length]
   445→
   446→            # Create labels
   447→            chosen_sequence_tokens = {
   448→                k: chosen_tokens[f"prompt_{k}"] + chosen_tokens[k] for k in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]
   449→            }
   450→            rejected_sequence_tokens = {
   451→                k: rejected_tokens[f"prompt_{k}"] + rejected_tokens[k] for k in ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]
   452→            }
   453→            chosen_sequence_tokens["labels"] = chosen_sequence_tokens["input_ids"][:]
   454→            chosen_sequence_tokens["labels"][: len(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])] = [
   455→                self.label_pad_token_id
   456→            ] * len(chosen_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   457→            rejected_sequence_tokens["labels"] = rejected_sequence_tokens["input_ids"][:]
   458→            rejected_sequence_tokens["labels"][: len(rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])] = [
   459→                self.label_pad_token_id
   460→            ] * len(rejected_tokens["prompt_input_ids"])
   461→
   462→            for k, toks in {
   463→                "chosen_": chosen_sequence_tokens,
   464→                "rejected_": rejected_sequence_tokens,
   465→                "": prompt_tokens,
   466→            }.items():
   467→                for type_key, tokens in toks.items():
   468→                    if type_key == "token_type_ids":
   469→                        continue
   470→                    batch[f"{k}{type_key}"] = tokens
   471→
   472→        else:
   473→            chosen_tokens = self.tokenizer(
   474→                chosen, truncation=True, max_length=self.max_target_length, add_special_tokens=True
   475→            )
   476→            rejected_tokens = self.tokenizer(
   477→                rejected, truncation=True, max_length=self.max_target_length, add_special_tokens=True
   478→            )
   479→            prompt_tokens = self.tokenizer(
   480→                prompt, truncation=True, max_length=self.max_prompt_length, add_special_tokens=True
   481→            )
   482→
   483→            batch["chosen_labels"] = chosen_tokens["input_ids"]
   484→            batch["rejected_labels"] = rejected_tokens["input_ids"]
   485→            batch["prompt_input_ids"] = prompt_tokens["input_ids"]
   486→            batch["prompt_attention_mask"] = prompt_tokens["attention_mask"]
   487→
   488→            if model is not None and hasattr(model, "prepare_decoder_input_ids_from_labels"):
   489→                batch["rejected_decoder_input_ids"] = model.prepare_decoder_input_ids_from_labels(
   490→                    labels=torch.tensor(batch["rejected_labels"])
   491→                )
   492→                batch["chosen_decoder_input_ids"] = model.prepare_decoder_input_ids_from_labels(
   493→                    labels=torch.tensor(batch["chosen_labels"])
   494→                )
   495→
   496→        return batch

   498→    @staticmethod
   499→    def concatenated_inputs(
   500→        batch: Dict[str, Union[List, torch.LongTensor]],
   501→        is_encoder_decoder: bool = False,
   502→        label_pad_token_id: int = -100,
   503→        padding_value: int = 0,
   504→        device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
   505→    ) -> Dict[str, torch.LongTensor]:
   506→        """Concatenate the chosen and rejected inputs into a single tensor.
   507→
   508→        Args:
   509→            batch: A batch of data. Must contain the keys 'chosen_input_ids' and 'rejected_input_ids', which are tensors of shape (batch_size, sequence_length).
   510→            is_encoder_decoder: Whether the model is an encoder-decoder model.
   511→            label_pad_token_id: The label pad token id.
   512→            padding_value: The padding value to use for the concatenated inputs_ids.
   513→            device: The device for the concatenated inputs.
   514→
   515→        Returns:
   516→            A dictionary containing the concatenated inputs under the key 'concatenated_input_ids'.
   517→        """
   518→        concatenated_batch = {}
   519→
   520→        if is_encoder_decoder:
   521→            max_length = max(batch["chosen_labels"].shape[1], batch["rejected_labels"].shape[1])
   522→        else:
   523→            max_length = max(batch["chosen_input_ids"].shape[1], batch["rejected_input_ids"].shape[1])
   524→
   525→        for k in batch:
   526→            if k.startswith("chosen") and isinstance(batch[k], torch.Tensor):
   527→                if "labels" in k or is_encoder_decoder:
   528→                    pad_value = label_pad_token_id
   529→                elif k.endswith("_input_ids"):
   530→                    pad_value = padding_value
   531→                elif k.endswith("_attention_mask"):
   532→                    pad_value = 0
   533→                concatenated_key = k.replace("chosen", "concatenated")
   534→                concatenated_batch[concatenated_key] = pad_to_length(batch[k], max_length, pad_value=pad_value)
   535→        for k in batch:
   536→            if k.startswith("rejected") and isinstance(batch[k], torch.Tensor):
   537→                if "labels" in k or is_encoder_decoder:
   538→                    pad_value = label_pad_token_id
   539→                elif k.endswith("_input_ids"):
   540→                    pad_value = padding_value
   541→                elif k.endswith("_attention_mask"):
   542→                    pad_value = 0
   543→                concatenated_key = k.replace("rejected", "concatenated")
   544→                concatenated_batch[concatenated_key] = torch.cat(
   545→                    (
   546→                        concatenated_batch[concatenated_key],
   547→                        pad_to_length(batch[k], max_length, pad_value=pad_value),
   548→                    ),
   549→                    dim=0,
   550→                ).to(device=device)
   551→
   552→        if is_encoder_decoder:
   553→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_input_ids"] = batch["prompt_input_ids"].repeat(2, 1).to(device=device)
   554→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_attention_mask"] = (
   555→                batch["prompt_attention_mask"].repeat(2, 1).to(device=device)
   556→            )
   557→
   558→        return concatenated_batch

   560→    def simpo_loss(
   561→        self,
   562→        policy_chosen_logps: torch.FloatTensor,
   563→        policy_rejected_logps: torch.FloatTensor,
   564→    ) -> Tuple[torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor]:
   565→        """Compute the SimPO loss for a batch of policy model log probabilities.
   566→
   567→        Args:
   568→            policy_chosen_logps: Log probabilities of the policy model for the chosen responses. Shape: (batch_size,)
   569→            policy_rejected_logps: Log probabilities of the policy model for the rejected responses. Shape: (batch_size,)
   570→
   571→        Returns:
   572→            A tuple of three tensors: (losses, chosen_rewards, rejected_rewards).
   573→            The losses tensor contains the SimPO loss for each example in the batch.
   574→            The chosen_rewards and rejected_rewards tensors contain the rewards for the chosen and rejected responses, respectively.
   575→        """
   576→
   577→        return losses, chosen_rewards, rejected_rewards
   578→
   579→    def concatenated_forward(
   580→        self, model: nn.Module, batch: Dict[str, Union[List, torch.LongTensor]]
   581→    ) -> Tuple[torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor, torch.FloatTensor]:
   582→        """Run the given model on the given batch of inputs, concatenating the chosen and rejected inputs together.
   583→
   584→        We do this to avoid doing two forward passes, because it's faster for FSDP.
   585→        """
   586→        concatenated_batch = self.concatenated_inputs(
   587→            batch,
   588→            is_encoder_decoder=self.is_encoder_decoder,
   589→            label_pad_token_id=self.label_pad_token_id,
   590→            padding_value=self.padding_value,
   591→            device=self.accelerator.device,
   592→        )
   593→        len_chosen = batch["chosen_labels"].shape[0]
   594→
   595→        model_kwargs = (
   596→            {
   597→                "labels": concatenated_batch["concatenated_labels"],
   598→                "decoder_input_ids": concatenated_batch.pop("concatenated_decoder_input_ids", None),
   599→            }
   600→            if self.is_encoder_decoder
   601→            else {}
   602→        )
   603→
   604→        all_logits = model(
   605→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_input_ids"],
   606→            attention_mask=concatenated_batch["concatenated_attention_mask"],
   607→            use_cache=False,
   608→            **model_kwargs,
   609→        ).logits
   610→
   611→        all_logps = self.get_batch_logps(
   612→            all_logits,
   613→            concatenated_batch["concatenated_labels"],
   614→            average_log_prob=True,
   615→            is_encoder_decoder=self.is_encoder_decoder,
   616→            label_pad_token_id=self.label_pad_token_id,
   617→        )
   618→
   619→        chosen_logps = all_logps[:len_chosen]
   620→        rejected_logps = all_logps[len_chosen:]
   621→
   622→        chosen_logits = all_logits[:len_chosen]
   623→        rejected_logits = all_logits[len_chosen:]
   624→
   625→        chosen_labels = concatenated_batch["concatenated_labels"][:len_chosen]
   626→
   627→        return (chosen_logps, rejected_logps, chosen_logits, rejected_logits, chosen_labels)
   628→
   629→    @staticmethod
   630→    def get_batch_logps(
   631→        logits: torch.FloatTensor,
   632→        labels: torch.LongTensor,
   633→        average_log_prob: bool = True,
   634→        label_pad_token_id: int = -100,
   635→        is_encoder_decoder: bool = False,
   636→    ) -> torch.FloatTensor:
   637→        """Compute the log probabilities of the given labels under the given logits.
   638→
   639→        Args:
   640→            logits: Logits of the model (unnormalized). Shape: (batch_size, sequence_length, vocab_size)
   641→            labels: Labels for which to compute the log probabilities. Label tokens with a value of label_pad_token_id are ignored. Shape: (batch_size, sequence_length)
   642→            average_log_prob: If True, return the average log probability per (non-masked) token. Otherwise, return the sum of the log probabilities of the (non-masked) tokens.
   643→            label_pad_token_id: The label pad token id.
   644→            is_encoder_decoder: Whether the model is an encoder-decoder model.
   645→
   646→        Returns:
   647→            A tensor of shape (batch_size,) containing the average/sum log probabilities of the given labels under the given logits.
   648→        """
   649→        if logits.shape[:-1] != labels.shape:
   650→            raise ValueError("Logits (batch and sequence length dim) and labels must have the same shape.")
   651→
   652→        if not is_encoder_decoder:
   653→            labels = labels[:, 1:].clone()
   654→            logits = logits[:, :-1, :]
   655→        loss_mask = labels != label_pad_token_id
   656→
   657→        # dummy token; we'll ignore the losses on these tokens later
   658→        labels[labels == label_pad_token_id] = 0
   659→
   660→        per_token_logps = torch.gather(logits.log_softmax(-1), dim=2, index=labels.unsqueeze(2)).squeeze(2)
   661→
   662→        if average_log_prob:
   663→            return (per_token_logps * loss_mask).sum(-1) / loss_mask.sum(-1)
   664→        else:
   665→            return (per_token_logps * loss_mask).sum(-1)
   666→
   667→    def get_batch_loss_metrics(
   668→        self,
   669→        model,
   670→        batch: Dict[str, Union[List, torch.LongTensor]],
   671→        train_eval: Literal["train", "eval"] = "train",
   672→    ):
   673→        """Compute the SimPO loss and other metrics for the given batch of inputs for train or test."""
   674→        metrics = {}
   675→        prefix = "eval_" if train_eval == "eval" else ""
   676→
   677→        (
   678→            policy_chosen_logps,
   679→            policy_rejected_logps,
   680→            policy_chosen_logits,
   681→            policy_rejected_logits,
   682→            chosen_labels,
   683→        ) = self.concatenated_forward(model, batch)
   684→
   685→        losses, chosen_rewards, rejected_rewards = self.simpo_loss(
   686→            policy_chosen_logps,
   687→            policy_rejected_logps,
   688→        )
   689→
   690→        loss = losses.mean()
   691→
   692→        if self.sft_weight > 0.0:
   693→            if not self.is_encoder_decoder:
   694→                policy_chosen_logits = policy_chosen_logits[..., :-1, :].contiguous()
   695→                chosen_labels = chosen_labels[..., 1:].clone()
   696→            loss_func = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
   697→            sft_loss = loss_func(policy_chosen_logits.view(-1, policy_chosen_logits.shape[-1]), chosen_labels.view(-1))
   698→            loss = self.sft_weight * sft_loss + loss
   699→            metrics[f"{prefix}sft_loss"] = sft_loss.detach().cpu()
   700→        
   701→        reward_accuracies = (chosen_rewards > rejected_rewards).float()
   702→
   703→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/chosen"] = chosen_rewards.mean().cpu()
   704→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/rejected"] = rejected_rewards.mean().cpu()
   705→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/accuracies"] = reward_accuracies.mean().cpu()
   706→        metrics[f"{prefix}rewards/margins"] = (chosen_rewards - rejected_rewards).mean().cpu()
   707→        metrics[f"{prefix}logps/rejected"] = policy_rejected_logps.detach().mean().cpu()
   708→        metrics[f"{prefix}logps/chosen"] = policy_chosen_logps.detach().mean().cpu()
   709→        metrics[f"{prefix}logits/rejected"] = policy_rejected_logits.detach().mean().cpu()
   710→        metrics[f"{prefix}logits/chosen"] = policy_chosen_logits.detach().mean().cpu()
   711→
   712→        return loss, metrics
   713→
   714→    def compute_loss(
   715→        self,
   716→        model: Union[PreTrainedModel, nn.Module],
   717→        inputs: Dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, Any]],
   718→        return_outputs=False,
   719→    ) -> Union[torch.Tensor, Tuple[torch.Tensor, Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]]:
   720→        if not self.use_dpo_data_collator:
   721→            warnings.warn(
   722→                "compute_loss is only implemented for DPODataCollatorWithPadding, and you passed a datacollator that is different than "
   723→                "DPODataCollatorWithPadding - you might see unexpected behavior. Alternatively, you can implement your own prediction_step method if you are using a custom data collator"
   724→            )
   725→
   726→        compute_loss_context_manager = torch.cuda.amp.autocast if self._peft_has_been_casted_to_bf16 else nullcontext
   727→
   728→        with compute_loss_context_manager():
   729→            loss, metrics = self.get_batch_loss_metrics(model, inputs, train_eval="train")
   730→
   731→        # force log the metrics
   732→        self.store_metrics(metrics, train_eval="train")
   733→
   734→        if return_outputs:
   735→            return (loss, metrics)
   736→        return loss

   738→    def get_batch_samples(self, model, batch: Dict[str, torch.LongTensor]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
   739→        """Generate samples from the model and reference model for the given batch of inputs."""
   740→
   741→        # If one uses `generate_during_eval` with peft + bf16, we need to explicitly call generate with
   742→        # the torch cuda amp context manager as some hidden states are silently casted to full precision.
   743→        generate_context_manager = nullcontext if not self._peft_has_been_casted_to_bf16 else torch.cuda.amp.autocast
   744→
   745→        with generate_context_manager():
   746→            policy_output = model.generate(
   747→                input_ids=batch["prompt_input_ids"],
   748→                attention_mask=batch["prompt_attention_mask"],
   749→                max_length=self.max_length,
   750→                do_sample=True,
   751→                pad_token_id=self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
   752→            )
   753→
   754→        policy_output = pad_to_length(policy_output, self.max_length, self.tokenizer.pad_token_id)
   755→        policy_output_decoded = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(policy_output, skip_special_tokens=True)
   756→
   757→        return policy_output_decoded

   759→    def prediction_step(
   760→        self,
   761→        model: Union[PreTrainedModel, nn.Module],
   762→        inputs: Dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, Any]],
   763→        prediction_loss_only: bool,
   764→        ignore_keys: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   765→    ):
   766→        if not self.use_dpo_data_collator:
   767→            warnings.warn(
   768→                "prediction_step is only implemented for DPODataCollatorWithPadding, and you passed a datacollator that is different than "
   769→                "DPODataCollatorWithPadding - you might see unexpected behavior. Alternatively, you can implement your own prediction_step method if you are using a custom data collator"
   770→            )
   771→        if ignore_keys is None:
   772→            if hasattr(model, "config"):
   773→                ignore_keys = getattr(model.config, "keys_to_ignore_at_inference", [])
   774→            else:
   775→                ignore_keys = []
   776→
   777→        prediction_context_manager = torch.cuda.amp.autocast if self._peft_has_been_casted_to_bf16 else nullcontext
   778→
   779→        with torch.no_grad(), prediction_context_manager():
   780→            loss, metrics = self.get_batch_loss_metrics(model, inputs, train_eval="eval")
   781→
   782→        # force log the metrics
   783→        self.store_metrics(metrics, train_eval="eval")
   784→
   785→        if prediction_loss_only:
   786→            return (loss.detach(), None, None)
   787→
   788→        # logits for the chosen and rejected samples from model
   789→        logits_dict = {
   790→            "eval_logits/chosen": metrics["eval_logits/chosen"],
   791→            "eval_logits/rejected": metrics["eval_logits/rejected"],
   792→        }
   793→        logits = tuple(v.unsqueeze(dim=0) for k, v in logits_dict.items() if k not in ignore_keys)
   794→        logits = torch.stack(logits).mean(axis=1).to(self.accelerator.device)
   795→        labels = torch.zeros(logits.shape[0], device=self.accelerator.device)
   796→
   797→        return (loss.detach(), logits, labels)

   799→    def store_metrics(self, metrics: Dict[str, float], train_eval: Literal["train", "eval"] = "train") -> None:
   800→        for key, value in metrics.items():
   801→            self._stored_metrics[train_eval][key].append(value)

   803→    def evaluation_loop(
   804→        self,
   805→        dataloader: DataLoader,
   806→        description: str,
   807→        prediction_loss_only: Optional[bool] = None,

DPO supports multiple loss types including 'sigmoid', 'hinge', 'ipo', and 'kto_pair'.

The beta parameter is a temperature parameter typically in the range of 0.1 to 0.5, and label_smoothing is a parameter encoding uncertainty about the labels. The label_smoothing parameter in DPOConfig models the probability of existing label noise, and should be set to a value between 0.0 and 0.5.

# DPO Trainer

[![model badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/All_models-DPO-blue)](https://huggingface.co/models?other=dpo,trl) [![model badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/smol_course-Chapter_2-yellow)](https://github.com/huggingface/smol-course/tree/main/2_preference_alignment)

## Overview

TRL supports the DPO Trainer for training language models from preference data, as described in the paper [Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model](https://huggingface.co/papers/2305.18290) by [Rafael Rafailov](https://huggingface.co/rmrafailov), Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, [Stefano Ermon](https://huggingface.co/ermonste), [Christopher D. Manning](https://huggingface.co/manning), [Chelsea Finn](https://huggingface.co/cbfinn).

The abstract from the paper is the following:

> While large-scale unsupervised language models (LMs) learn broad world knowledge and some reasoning skills, achieving precise control of their behavior is difficult due to the completely unsupervised nature of their training. Existing methods for gaining such steerability collect human labels of the relative quality of model generations and fine-tune the unsupervised LM to align with these preferences, often with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, RLHF is a complex and often unstable procedure, first fitting a reward model that reflects the human preferences, and then fine-tuning the large unsupervised LM using reinforcement learning to maximize this estimated reward without drifting too far from the original model. In this paper we introduce a new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that enables extraction of the corresponding optimal policy in closed form, allowing us to solve the standard RLHF problem with only a simple classification loss. The resulting algorithm, which we call Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), is stable, performant, and computationally lightweight, eliminating the need for sampling from the LM during fine-tuning or performing significant hyperparameter tuning. Our experiments show that DPO can fine-tune LMs to align with human preferences as well as or better than existing methods. Notably, fine-tuning with DPO exceeds PPO-based RLHF in ability to control sentiment of generations, and matches or improves response quality in summarization and single-turn dialogue while being substantially simpler to implement and train.

The first step is to train an SFT model, to ensure the data we train on is in-distribution for the DPO algorithm.

Then, fine-tuning a language model via DPO consists of two steps and is easier than [PPO](ppo_trainer):

1. **Data collection**: Gather a [preference dataset](dataset_formats#preference) with positive and negative selected pairs of generation, given a prompt.
2. **Optimization**: Maximize the log-likelihood of the DPO loss directly.

This process is illustrated in the sketch below (from [Figure 1 of the DPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2305.18290)):

![Figure 1 DPO](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/assets/49240599/9150fac6-3d88-4ca2-8ec6-2a6f3473216d)

Read more about DPO algorithm in the [original paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2305.18290).

## Quick start

This example demonstrates how to train a model using the DPO method. We use the [Qwen 0.5B model](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct) as the base model. We use the preference data from the [UltraFeedback dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openbmb/UltraFeedback). You can view the data in the dataset here:

Below is the script to train the model:

```python
# train_dpo.py
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import DPOConfig, DPOTrainer
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct")
train_dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/ultrafeedback_binarized", split="train")

training_args = DPOConfig(output_dir="Qwen2-0.5B-DPO")
trainer = DPOTrainer(model=model, args=training_args, processing_class=tokenizer, train_dataset=train_dataset)
trainer.train()
```

Execute the script using the following command:

```bash
accelerate launch train_dpo.py
```

Distributed across 8 GPUs, the training takes approximately 3 minutes. You can verify the training progress by checking the reward graph. An increasing trend in the reward margin indicates that the model is improving and generating better responses over time.

![](https://huggingface.co/datasets/trl-lib/documentation-images/resolve/main/dpo-qwen2-reward-margin.png)

To see how the [trained model](https://huggingface.co/trl-lib/Qwen2-0.5B-DPO) performs, you can use the [Transformers Chat CLI](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/quicktour#chat-with-text-generation-models).

It provides a repository of over 300, 000  pre-trained models in a variety of languages, enabling users to explore and utilize the latest techniques and technologies in the field of machine learning.

## Expected dataset type

DPO requires a [preference dataset](dataset_formats#preference). The [DPOTrainer](/docs/trl/main/en/bema_for_reference_model#trl.DPOTrainer) supports both [conversational](dataset_formats#conversational) and [standard](dataset_formats#standard) dataset formats. When provided with a conversational dataset, the trainer will automatically apply the chat template to the dataset.

Although the [DPOTrainer](/docs/trl/main/en/bema_for_reference_model#trl.DPOTrainer) supports both explicit and implicit prompts, we recommend using explicit prompts. If provided with an implicit prompt dataset, the trainer will automatically extract the prompt from the `"chosen"` and `"rejected"` columns. For more information, refer to the [preference style](dataset_formats#preference) section.

### Special considerations for vision-language models

The [DPOTrainer](/docs/trl/main/en/bema_for_reference_model#trl.DPOTrainer) supports fine-tuning vision-language models (VLMs). For these models, a vision dataset is required. To learn more about the specific format for vision datasets, refer to the [Vision dataset format](dataset_formats#vision-datasets) section.

Additionally, unlike standard text-based models where a `tokenizer` is used, for VLMs, you should replace the `tokenizer` with a `processor`.

```diff
- model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id)
+ model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(model_id)

- tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
+ processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)

  trainer = DPOTrainer(
      model,
      args=training_args,
      train_dataset=train_dataset,
-     processing_class=tokenizer,
+     processing_class=processor,
)
```

For a complete example of fine-tuning a vision-language model, refer to the script in [`examples/scripts/dpo_vlm.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/examples/scripts/dpo_vlm.py).

## Example script

We provide an example script to train a model using the DPO method. The script is available in [`trl/scripts/dpo.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/trl/scripts/dpo.py)

To test the DPO script with the [Qwen2 0.5B model](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct) on the [UltraFeedback dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/trl-lib/ultrafeedback_binarized), run the following command:

```bash
accelerate launch trl/scripts/dpo.py \
    --model_name_or_path Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct \
    --dataset_name trl-lib/ultrafeedback_binarized \
    --num_train_epochs 1 \
    --output_dir Qwen2-0.5B-DPO
```

## Logged metrics

While training and evaluating, we record the following reward metrics:

- `rewards/chosen`: the mean difference between the log probabilities of the policy model and the reference model for the chosen responses scaled by beta
- `rewards/rejected`: the mean difference between the log probabilities of the policy model and the reference model for the rejected responses scaled by beta
- `rewards/accuracies`: mean of how often the chosen rewards are > than the corresponding rejected rewards
- `rewards/margins`: the mean difference between the chosen and corresponding rejected rewards

## Loss functions

The DPO algorithm supports several loss functions. The loss function can be set using the `loss_type` parameter in the [DPOConfig](/docs/trl/main/en/dpo_trainer#trl.DPOConfig). The following loss functions are supported:

| `loss_type=` | Description |
| --- | --- |

| `"hinge"` | The [RSO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2309.06657) authors propose to use a hinge loss on the normalized likelihood from the [SLiC](https://huggingface.co/papers/2305.10425) paper. In this case, the `beta` is the reciprocal of the margin. |
| `"ipo"` | The [IPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2310.12036) authors provide a deeper theoretical understanding of the DPO algorithms and identify an issue with overfitting and propose an alternative loss. As per the paper the loss is averaged over log-likelihoods of the completion (unlike DPO which is summed only). |
| `"exo_pair"` | The [EXO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2402.00856) authors propose to minimize the reverse KL instead of the negative log-sigmoid loss of DPO which corresponds to forward KL. Setting non-zero `label_smoothing` (default `1e-3`) leads to a simplified version of EXO on pair-wise preferences (see Eqn. (16) of the [EXO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2402.00856)). | `"nca_pair"` | The [NCA](https://huggingface.co/papers/2402.05369) authors shows that NCA optimizes the absolute likelihood for each response rather than the relative likelihood. |
| `"robust"` | The [Robust DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2403.00409) authors propose an unbiased estimate of the DPO loss that is robust to preference noise in the data. Like in cDPO, it assumes that the preference labels are noisy with some probability. In this approach, the `label_smoothing` parameter in the [DPOConfig](/docs/trl/main/en/dpo_trainer#trl.DPOConfig) is used to model the probability of existing label noise. To apply this conservative loss, set `label_smoothing` to a value greater than 0.0 (between 0.0 and 0.5; the default is 0.0) |
| `"bco_pair"` | The [BCO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.04656) authors train a binary classifier whose logit serves as a reward so that the classifier maps {prompt, chosen completion} pairs to 1 and {prompt, rejected completion} pairs to 0. The implementation approximates this algorithm by employing hard label probabilities, assigning 1 to the winner and 0 to the loser. |

Specifically, `loss_type="aot"` is appropriate for paired datasets, where each prompt has both chosen and rejected responses; `loss_type="aot_pair"` is for unpaired datasets. In a nutshell, `loss_type="aot"` ensures that the log-likelihood ratio of chosen to rejected of the aligned model has higher quantiles than that ratio for the reference model. `loss_type="aot_pair"` ensures that the chosen reward is higher on all quantiles than the rejected reward. ### Multi-loss combinations

The DPO trainer supports combining multiple loss functions with different weights, enabling more sophisticated optimization strategies. This is particularly useful for implementing algorithms like MPO (Mixed Preference Optimization). MPO is a training approach that combines multiple optimization objectives, as described in the paper [Enhancing the Reasoning Ability of Multimodal Large Language Models via Mixed Preference Optimization](https://huggingface.co/papers/2411.10442).

To combine multiple losses, specify the loss types and corresponding weights as lists:

```python
# MPO: Combines DPO (sigmoid) for preference and BCO (bco_pair) for quality
training_args = DPOConfig(
    loss_type=["sigmoid", "bco_pair", "sft"],  # Loss types to combine
    loss_weights=[0.8, 0.2, 1.0]  # Corresponding weights, as used in the MPO paper
)
```

If `loss_weights` is not provided, all loss types will have equal weights (1.0 by default).

### Label smoothing

The [cDPO](https://ericmitchell.ai/cdpo.pdf) is a tweak on the DPO loss where we assume that the preference labels are noisy with some probability. In this approach, the `label_smoothing` parameter in the [DPOConfig](/docs/trl/main/en/dpo_trainer#trl.DPOConfig) is used to model the probability of existing label noise. To apply this conservative loss, set `label_smoothing` to a value greater than 0.0 (between 0.0 and 0.5; the default is 0.0).

### Syncing the reference model

The [TR-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.09656) paper suggests syncing the reference model weights after every `ref_model_sync_steps` steps of SGD with weight `ref_model_mixup_alpha` during DPO training. To toggle this callback use the `sync_ref_model=True` in the [DPOConfig](/docs/trl/main/en/dpo_trainer#trl.DPOConfig).

### RPO loss

The [RPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.19733) paper implements an iterative preference tuning algorithm using a loss related to the RPO loss in this [paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2405.16436) that essentially consists of a weighted SFT loss on the chosen preferences together with the DPO loss. To use this loss, include `"sft"` in the `loss_type` list in the [DPOConfig](/docs/trl/main/en/dpo_trainer#trl.DPOConfig) and set its weight in `loss_weights`.

> [!WARNING]
> The old implementation of RPO loss in TRL used the `rpo_alpha` parameter. This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in 0.29.0; instead.

### WPO loss

The [WPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2406.11827) paper adapts off-policy data to resemble on-policy data more closely by reweighting preference pairs according to their probability under the current policy. To use this method, set the `use_weighting` flag to `True` in the [DPOConfig](/docs/trl/main/en/dpo_trainer#trl.DPOConfig).

### LD-DPO loss

The [LD-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2409.06411) paper decomposes the portion of the response that exceeds the desired length into two components — human-like preferences and verbosity preference — based on a mixing coefficient  \\( \alpha \\). To use this method, set the `ld_alpha` in the [DPOConfig](/docs/trl/main/en/dpo_trainer#trl.DPOConfig) to an appropriate value. The paper suggests setting this value between `0.0` and `1.0`.

### For Mixture of Experts Models: Enabling the auxiliary loss

MOEs are the most efficient if the load is about equally distributed between experts.  
To ensure that we train MOEs similarly during preference-tuning, it is beneficial to add the auxiliary loss from the load balancer to the final loss.

This option is enabled by setting `output_router_logits=True` in the model config (e.g. [MixtralConfig](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/mixtral#transformers.MixtralConfig)).  
To scale how much the auxiliary loss contributes to the total loss, use the hyperparameter `router_aux_loss_coef=...` (default: `0.001`) in the model config.

### Rapid Experimentation for DPO

RapidFire AI is an open-source experimentation engine that sits on top of TRL and lets you launch multiple DPO configurations at once, even on a single GPU. Instead of trying configurations sequentially, RapidFire lets you **see all their learning curves earlier, stop underperforming runs, and clone promising ones with new settings in flight** without restarting. For more information, see [RapidFire AI Integration](rapidfire_integration).

## Accelerate DPO fine-tuning using `unsloth`

You can further accelerate QLoRA / LoRA (2x faster, 60% less memory) using the [`unsloth`](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth) library that is fully compatible with `SFTTrainer`. Currently `unsloth` supports only Llama (Yi, TinyLlama, Qwen, Deepseek etc) and Mistral architectures. Some benchmarks for DPO listed below:

| GPU | Model | Dataset | 🤗 | 🤗 + FlashAttention 2 | 🦥 Unsloth | 🦥 VRAM saved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A100 40G | Zephyr 7b | Ultra Chat | 1x | 1.24x | **1.88x** | -11.6% |
| Tesla T4 | Zephyr 7b | Ultra Chat | 1x | 1.09x | **1.55x** | -18.6% |

First install `unsloth` according to the [official documentation](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth). Once installed, you can incorporate unsloth into your workflow in a very simple manner; instead of loading `AutoModelForCausalLM`, you just need to load a `FastLanguageModel` as follows:

```diff
  from datasets import load_dataset

+ from unsloth import FastLanguageModel

- model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct")
- tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct")
+ model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct")
+ model = FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model(model)
  train_dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/ultrafeedback_binarized", split="train")

- training_args = DPOConfig(output_dir="Qwen2-0.5B-DPO")
+ training_args = DPOConfig(output_dir="Qwen2-0.5B-DPO", bf16=True)
  trainer = DPOTrainer(model=model, args=training_args, processing_class=tokenizer, train_dataset=train_dataset)
  trainer.train()

```

The saved model is fully compatible with Hugging Face's transformers library. Learn more about unsloth in their [official repository](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth).

## Reference model considerations with PEFT

You have three main options (plus several variants) for how the reference model works when using PEFT, assuming the model that you would like to further enhance with DPO was tuned using (Q)LoRA.

1. Simply create two instances of the model, each loading your adapter - works fine but is very inefficient.
2. Merge the adapter into the base model, create another adapter on top, then leave the `ref_model` param null, in which case DPOTrainer will unload the adapter for reference inference - efficient, but has potential downsides discussed below.
3. Load the adapter twice with different names, then use `set_adapter` during training to swap between the adapter being DPO'd and the reference adapter - slightly less efficient compared to 2 (~adapter size VRAM overhead), but avoids the pitfalls.

### Downsides to merging QLoRA before DPO (approach 2)

As suggested by [Benjamin Marie](https://medium.com/@bnjmn_marie/dont-merge-your-lora-adapter-into-a-4-bit-llm-65b6da287997), the best option for merging QLoRA adapters is to first dequantize the base model, then merge the adapter. Something similar to [this script](https://github.com/jondurbin/qlora/blob/main/qmerge.py).

However, after using this approach, you will have an unquantized base model. Therefore, to use QLoRA for DPO, you will need to re-quantize the merged model or use the unquantized merge (resulting in higher memory demand).

### Using option 3 - load the adapter twice

To avoid the downsides with option 2, you can load your fine-tuned adapter into the model twice, with different names, and set the model/ref adapter names in [DPOTrainer](/docs/trl/main/en/bema_for_reference_model#trl.DPOTrainer).

For example:

```python
# Load the base model.
bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    llm_int8_threshold=6.0,
    llm_int8_has_fp16_weight=False,
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "mistralai/mixtral-8x7b-v0.1",
    load_in_4bit=True,
    quantization_config=bnb_config,
    attn_implementation="kernels-community/flash-attn2",
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map="auto",
)

# Load the adapter.
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(
    model,
    "/path/to/peft",
    is_trainable=True,
    adapter_name="train",
)
# Load the adapter a second time, with a different name, which will be our reference model.
model.load_adapter("/path/to/peft", adapter_name="reference")

# Initialize the trainer, without a ref_model param.
training_args = DPOConfig(
    model_adapter_name="train",
    ref_adapter_name="reference",
)
dpo_trainer = DPOTrainer(
    model,
    args=training_args,
    ...
)
```

    policy_chosen_logps: torch.FloatTensor,
    policy_rejected_logps: torch.FloatTensor,

    if self.loss_type == "simpo":

            - F.logsigmoid(-self.beta * logits) * self.label_smoothing

        )

        losses = torch.relu(1 - self.beta * logits)
